title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page. A Tannakian category M of motives over k0 (char 0), with motivic Galois group G and Lie algebra g (the symbol read as 𝒱 in the previous transcription is surely 𝔤). K/k0 is an extension field. After choosing a trivialisation of the relevant torsor, the de Rham realisation over K carries a Gauss–Manin connection of the form ∇_X = θ_{0X} + ω(X). Here θ_0 is the trivial connection on V⊗_{k0}K, and the connection form ω: Dér(K/k0) → g_K = g⊗_{k0}K is K-linear. Integrability means dω(X∧Y) = ω([X,Y]) − [ω(X),ω(Y)].

Question. Given motives V, W, which k0-rational linear maps u: V_K → W_K that commute with Gauss–Manin (i.e. are horizontal) actually come from morphisms of motives?

This page answers it as follows.
- Being a morphism of motives amounts to u_K commuting with g_K (Tannakian description).
- By hypothesis u commutes with the θ_X, hence with the ω(X), X ∈ Dér(K/k0).
- Let h ⊂ g be the smallest k0-subspace such that h_K contains all ω(X).
- Linear-algebra step: the centraliser c ⊂ g of u is a k0-subspace (u is k0-rational). Since c_K contains the ω(X), minimality gives h ⊂ c, because forming intersections of subspaces commutes with base field extension. So u commutes with h.
- Hence it suffices that h = g. It would even suffice that the Lie algebra generated by h is g.
- Remark: one shows easily that h is already a Lie subalgebra. This is presumably via the integrability condition: [ω(X),ω(Y)] = ω([X,Y]) − θ_{0X}ω(Y) + θ_{0Y}ω(X), and the derivative terms stay in h_K because h is defined over k0.
- Alternatively one can replace h by the (possibly algebraic) Lie algebra it generates.

Purpose. This is a criterion for horizontal, k0-rational de Rham tensors to be motivic. Put differently, it compares the 'differential Galois' Lie algebra spanned by the Gauss–Manin connection form with the motivic Lie algebra. The next page turns to the comparison torsor P = Isom(T_ℓ, T_DR).
errors: Commuting with the Lie algebra g only gives invariance under the identity component G°. To conclude that u is a morphism of motives one also needs control of π0(G), e.g. G connected or an extra Galois argument. The page does not address this.

The condition h = g is very restrictive. For motives already defined over k0 one has ω = 0, so h = 0. In general h only sees the 'varying' part, analogous to the differential Galois / monodromy group, which is a normal subgroup of, but usually smaller than, the motivic group. The criterion is therefore sufficient but rarely applicable without a further argument.

The claim that h is 'easily' a Lie subalgebra needs an induction. h_K is spanned by the ω(X) together with their iterated derivatives under θ_0, and one must check that brackets of these derivatives stay in h_K. The argument is plausible via integrability but is not written out.

ideas.what: Gauss–Manin connection written as trivial connection plus a connection form valued in the Lie algebra of the motivic Galois group, ω ∈ Ω¹_{K/k0} ⊗ g
ideas.modern_name: Motivic nature of Gauss–Manin; the differential Galois group of GM is contained in (normal in) the motivic Galois group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz–Oda (1968) for algebraic GM; André (1990s, normality of differential Galois group in motivic group); Ayoub (2010s, motivic Galois group vs. relative periods)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA; GM ideas appear in Grothendieck's de Rham letters/IHES talks only in other forms

ideas.what: Criterion: horizontal k0-rational maps commute with the smallest k0-subspace h whose K-extension contains the connection form's values; if h (or the Lie algebra it generates) is g, horizontal maps are motivic
ideas.modern_name: Variational/'principle B'-type criterion; theorem of the fixed part for motivic Galois groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Principle B, 1982), André (theorem of the fixed part, motivated cycles, 1992–1996)

ideas.what: Field-of-definition / descent of subspaces: smallest k0-form h with ω(X) ∈ h_K
ideas.modern_name: Field of definition of a K-subspace

missed.claim: Already in 1965 Grothendieck treats the Gauss–Manin connection form as valued in the Lie algebra of the motivic Galois group. He uses it to decide when horizontal k0-rational tensors are motivic, which anticipates the later comparison of differential Galois groups with motivic Galois groups.
missed.quote: Soit 𝔥 ⊂ 𝔤 le plus petit sous-espace vectoriel de 𝔤 tel que 𝔥_K contienne les ω(X) ... il suffit que 𝔥 = 𝔤 pour pouvoir conclure
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows that the André/Ayoub line of thought (differential Galois group of GM vs. motivic Galois group, relative period conjectures) was envisaged by Grothendieck in the founding period of motivic Galois theory. This is of historical interest. It is not a new theorem, and the criterion as stated is weaker than later results.

deep.surprise_reason: Early (1965) explicit link between Gauss–Manin connection forms and the motivic Lie algebra, with a clean criterion for horizontal tensors to be motivic. The mathematics is elementary and was later superseded and credited to Deligne, André and Ayoub. The novelty is chiefly historical.
transcription_corrections: 'w(x)' should be ω(X) (connection form), and '(x ∈ Div(H/k0))' should be '(X ∈ Dér(K/k0))'.

The N.B. likely reads '(N.B. Il suffirait que l'algèbre de Lie engendrée par 𝔥 dans 𝔤 soit 𝔤, mais en fait on montrerait facilement que 𝔥 est déjà une sous-algèbre de Lie ....)' rather than 'Je n'utilise pas que ...'.
The last sentence probably reads 'Ou bien on remplace 𝔥 par la sous-algèbre de Lie (algébrique?) qu'elle engendre' (uncertain).
'u commute à 𝔥' at line 6 is correct; the struck symbol before it is a crossed-out letter.
On the previous page, '𝒱' / '𝒱_K' should be read as the Lie algebra 𝔤 / 𝔤_K.
